lookalikes.id: outside: circuit voltage-divider effects in three-terminal conductance

questions: How many devices did you measure with the TGP, and how many passed? You show six, four passing, and write "Indeed, we have measured devices in which we were not able to find a topological phase" (pp. 22 to 23).
Why were the others set aside? How many did the pinch-off health check (p. 12) or the n2D,int specification remove, and why were E and F the failing devices shown?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown: Vp outside the 30 mV Stage 1 window, Vp below −1.1580 V for device B (p. 25), fields above 2.5 T, and field angles off the wire axis (p. 19)?

What does the second-best device or dataset look like? Device A "regularly passed the TGP, but also failed sometimes" (p. 22): how many Stage 2 runs did each device get, and could you show a failing one?

Gth is set from the maximum non-local conductance found "scanning over all B for each Vp" (p. 39), and in simulation restricting the field to B ⩽ 2.5 T changed one outcome (p. 41). Could you rerun the released code on each measured dataset with the field, bias and Vp windows, resolution and cutter subsets varied, and report what changes?

Did you scan the cutters past the 0.1 to 1 e²/h window toward pinch-off, at zero and finite field, for Coulomb resonances of a junction dot, and do the SOI2 peaks survive changes of the outer plungers or helper gates?
Has the TGP been run on simulated trivial wires built to mimic a gap closing and reopening (smooth potentials, a bulk Andreev band), and did simulations and measurements use the same code version?
